title: Helm, GitOps and local clusters
summary: Package manifests, deploy them from Git, and practise on your laptop.

steps.title: Helm
body: Copy-pasting YAML for dev, test and prod drifts. **Helm** packages manifests as a **chart** with templates and a **values** file:
helm install shop ./shop-api -n shop -f values-prod.yaml --set image.tag=1.5
helm template ./shop-api -f values-prod.yaml      render locally, apply nothing

Values merge in order, later wins: chart `values.yaml` < each `-f` file in order < `--set`. A deployed chart is a **release**; each upgrade is a numbered **revision** you can roll back to. (Kustomize is the template-free alternative: a base plus per-environment patches, built into `kubectl apply -k`.)

steps.prompt: `values.yaml` has `replicaCount: 2`, `values-prod.yaml` has `replicaCount: 4`, and you run `helm upgrade shop ./chart -f values-prod.yaml --set replicaCount=6`. How many replicas?
steps.explain: `--set` beats files; later files beat earlier ones; the chart's own defaults come last.

steps.prompt: Complete the template line so the image tag comes from values.
steps.explain: Values from `values.yaml`, `-f` files and `--set` are all under `.Values`. `.Release.Name` and `.Chart.Version` hold other built-in data.

steps.title: GitOps
body: With **GitOps**, nobody runs `kubectl apply` or `helm upgrade` against production by hand. Instead:
developer --PR--> Git repo (manifests / Helm values)  <--watches--  Argo CD or Flux (in the cluster)
- Git is the desired state, with history, review and easy revert (`git revert` is your rollback).
- The agent **pulls** from inside the cluster, so CI needs no cluster credentials.
- Drift (someone's manual `kubectl edit`) is detected and reverted or flagged.
It is the reconcile loop from module 1, one level up: desired state is a Git commit.

steps.prompt: Someone runs `kubectl scale deploy/shop-api --replicas=1` in a cluster managed by Argo CD with self-heal on. Git says 4. What happens?
options: Argo CD sees the drift and sets replicas back to 4
The app stays at 1 until the next commit
steps.explain: If you really need 1, change it in Git. That is the point: the repo is the only way in.

steps.prompt: Match the local cluster tool to its description.
pairs: Kubernetes in Docker: each node is a container; fast to create and throw away, great in CI
a single-node cluster in a VM or container, with add-ons such as metrics-server and a local registry
a one-click cluster built into Docker Desktop's settings
a lightweight Kubernetes distribution, also popular on small edge devices

steps.title: Practising locally
body: kind load docker-image shop/api:dev --name dev     # use a locally built image without a registry

Local images and `imagePullPolicy`: with tag `:latest` the default is `Always`, which tries the registry and fails for an image that only exists on your machine (`ErrImagePull`). Use a specific tag (`:dev`), or set `imagePullPolicy: IfNotPresent`.
`kubectl port-forward` tunnels through the API server to a pod or Service, no Gateway or Ingress needed: the quickest way to reach a ClusterIP Service from your laptop.

steps.title: Merge Helm values
prompt: Write `Dictionary<string, string> Merge(List<Dictionary<string, string>> layers)` that merges flattened values (keys like `image.tag`) in order, later layers winning.

Then `string Render(string template, Dictionary<string, string> values)` replacing every `{{ .Values.KEY }}` (exactly one space inside each brace pair) with its value. Unknown keys render as an empty string, as Helm does.
starter: string Render(string template, Dictionary<string, string> values)
solution: foreach (var (k, v) in layer) result[k] = v;
string Render(string template, Dictionary<string, string> values)
template: Dojo.Eq("unknown key renders empty", "x=", Render("x={{ .Values.nope }}", dojoV));
Dojo.Eq("no placeholders", "kind: Service", Render("kind: Service", dojoV));
hints: Merge is the same overwrite loop as env precedence.
Find `{{ .Values.`, then the next ` }}`; the key is between them.
